nodes.title: Linux: app hard-freezes when it fires a notification with no notification daemon (sync libnotify call wedges UI thread)
nodes.body:
# Linux: Electron app hard-freezes when it fires a notification with no notification daemon

> Sync libnotify call wedges the UI thread. App must be SIGKILLed. Sound, GPU,
> and Wayland backend all falsified as causes. Bisected 2026-09-22.

## Environment

- OS: Arch-based (CachyOS), KDE Plasma 6.7.5, Wayland, single 1080p@144 panel
- App: `opencode-desktop` 1.18.32 (AppImage), Electron 42.3.3, native Wayland
  ozone (also reproduced with `--ozone-platform=x11`)
- Same repro on Discord desktop (Electron 42.11.1, native Wayland) — not
  app-specific
- `org.freedesktop.Notifications` ownerless on the session bus (Plasma never
  claims it; reproduced across reboots; 43 activation timeouts across 6 boots
  in retained journals)

## Repro (100% once the bus name is dead)

1. Ensure no notification daemon owns `org.freedesktop.Notifications`
   (verify: `busctl --user list | grep Notifications` shows `(activatable)`,
   no owner).
2. Leave the Electron app unfocused.
3. Trigger any app notification (e.g. task-completion ping, chat mention).
4. Refocus the app window.

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: notification delivered or silently dropped; app responsive.
- Actual: entire window dead — no repaint, no input, close button dead.
  Process alive but fully stalled; kill leaves a compositor ghost until the
  WM "not responding" prompt. Must SIGKILL + relaunch.

## Forensic evidence

- The frozen app logs the cause itself:
  `libnotify_notification.cc:61 notify_notification_show: Error calling
  StartServiceByName for org.freedesktop.Notifications: Timeout was reached`
- Bus-level proof, reproducible by hand:
  `busctl --user call org.freedesktop.Notifications … Notify …` →
  `Call failed: Connection timed out`. Activation spawns `plasma_waitforname`,
  which exits 1 (`Service was not registered within timeout`).
- `gstack` of the frozen renderer (18 threads): all parked in `epoll_wait` /
  `pthread_cond_wait` — no renderer deadlock; the wedge is the browser main
  thread inside the synchronous D-Bus call (browser/GPU procs unattachable
  under sandbox namespaces).
- Bisected out:
  - DSP/audio stack — froze with effects bypassed AND with the audio daemon
    fully killed (zero nodes in `pw-dump`).
  - Ozone backend — froze on both `wayland` and `x11`.
  - GPU — clean `dmesg`, no `i915` errors, compositor healthy, other apps
    unaffected.
- Discriminators: in-app mute does NOT prevent it (the notify call still
  fires); Do-Not-Disturb DOES (no call made). Running any daemon
  (`dunst`/`mako`) eliminates it.

## Upstream refs

- electron/electron#21912 — identical freeze, closed ("run dunst or another
  notification system").
- electron/electron#14006 — names `g_dbus_proxy_call_sync` in
  `libnotify_notification.cc` as the blocker (log shows Discord activating
  `org.freedesktop.Notifications`).
- KDE Discuss (Feb 2026) — Plasma-side refusal to host the name, messaging
  apps hanging for the 60s timeout, event-queue buildup.

## Suggested fix

Make the Linux notify path asynchronous (or time-bound with a short timeout)
so a missing/broken daemon degrades to a dropped notification instead of a
wedged UI thread; alternatively detect no-owner up front and skip the call.

---
*Created by AI model muse spark 1.3, opencode services.*

nodes.title: V8 Crash on Tier-up with WASM That Uses WASM exceptions
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42-x-y and 43-x-y

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 build 26200.9448

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

V8 should succeed in tiering-up WebAssembly, resulting in boosted performance. This should happen silently in the background, and of course, not crash.

### Actual Behavior

V8 crashes when attempting to tier-up _any_ WASM that includes WASM-based exception handling. Such WASM can be created by compiling via Emscripten with `--fwasm-exceptions`, not `--fexceptions` or no exception handling. To be clear, it's V8's tier-up operation that crashes, not the WebAssembly code.

The crash can appear to happen at random because Electron/V8 — not the code attempting to call the WASM — decides when to tier-up WASM.

Also, I saw this on both Windows and Mac.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Even though it's V8 that's crashing, the bug is in Electron code, not V8.

The upstream commit (written against V8 main, Aug 2026) declares the new
builtin as
`IF_WASM(TFS, WasmGetOwnProperty, NeedsContext{false}, kObject, kSymbol)`
and makes the Turboshaft descriptor `kNeedsContext = false`, passing two
arguments (`exception`, `symbol`) at three call sites in
`turboshaft-graph-interface.cc` (catch tag lookup ×2, exception value
unpacking) and in Liftoff.

On main, `NeedsContext` is `base::StrongAlias<NeedsContextTag, bool>`
(since V8 commit `a59996fbddf`, 2026-07-01), so `NeedsContext{false}` means
"no context". In V8 15.0 (and 14.8) that commit is absent and
`src/common/globals.h:3010` still reads
`enum class NeedsContext { kYes, kNo };`. Brace-initialising that enum from
`false` yields enumerator 0 = **kYes**. The line compiles and silently
inverts: the builtin's interface descriptor keeps a context parameter, so
the call descriptor has 3 parameters (`Descriptor:r1s0i4f0` in
`--trace-turbo-graph`) while every `Call` op only has 2 arguments
(`Call(#callee, #exception, #symbol)`).

In `patches/v8/cherry-pick-36079c36283a.patch` on 43-x-y and 42-x-y, the
`builtins-definitions.h` hunk must use the enum spelling of those branches:
```
-  IF_WASM(TFS, WasmGetOwnProperty, NeedsContext{false}, kObject, kSymbol)
+  IF_WASM(TFS, WasmGetOwnProperty, NeedsContext::kNo, kObject, kSymbol)
```
(or drop the backport on those lines). Electron 44.x and later are not affected.

nodes.title: feat: Googlebook platform support
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Google has just announced Googlebook, a new desktop platform:

https://googlebook.google/

For developers maintaining cross-platform Electron applications, there is currently no clear path for targeting Googlebook as a first-class platform.

As Googlebook is a desktop platform and may become relevant to existing Electron applications, it would be useful to clarify whether Electron intends to support Googlebook, and what form that support might take.

### Proposed Solution

Consider adding Googlebook as an officially supported Electron target platform, if technically feasible.

At this early stage, it would also be helpful to have guidance from the Electron team on whether Googlebook support is being considered, and whether it could be implemented through existing Linux support or would require a separate platform backend.

### Alternatives Considered

One possible alternative is running the existing Linux build of an Electron application through Googlebook's Linux environment, assuming this is supported and provides sufficient desktop integration.

Another option for applications with multiple frontends would be to maintain a separate Android-native or other Googlebook-compatible frontend. However, this would reduce the benefit of using Electron as a cross-platform desktop application framework.

### Additional Information

Googlebook was announced only about 20 minutes ago at the time of filing this issue, so I understand that it is extremely early and that the exact scope or feasibility of Electron support may not yet be known.

Official Googlebook website:

https://googlebook.google/

This issue is primarily intended to start a discussion about compatibility and the Electron project's plans for this new platform.

GoogleBook is android based, and Electron currently has no plans to support Android. The linux compat layer _might_ be able to run Electron but we do not know and are unlikely to make changes to specifically support that environment as it is developer only (not for typical googlebook users)

nodes.title: webview.findInPage hangs Electron when window contains an iframe
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist * [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. * [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) for this project. * [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.4.3 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 26.6 (25G72) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior Calling `webview.findInPage()` should return search results and keep the Electron application responsive. ### Actual Behavior A minimal Electron app becomes unresponsive after calling native `webview.findInPage()` when the same window contains an iframe. The call returns synchronously, but no `found-in-page` event arrives and the app stops processing its event loop. The user-visible result is a complete application hang. The attached reproduction searches for the single-character query `a`, but the same behavior occurs while rapidly navigating matches with Enter. The behavior reproduces with ordinary web pages as well as Google Docs. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/taozhou-glean/54bad8ed029baf3ef99f5a8f7ce7a560 ### Additional Information
In-depth investigation

I reproduced this in a clean Electron 44.4.3 app using one host-page iframe and one webview. The host iframe is intentionally tiny and hidden; removing it avoids the repro in the tested environment. The gist uses data URLs and does not depend on a specific website. Environment: - Electron 44.4.3 - Chromium 152.0.7977.130 - macOS 26.6 (25G72), arm64, Mac15,7 - Electron process launched from Ghostty During the hang, a macOS sample reported the Electron main process unresponsive for 40 seconds. The main process used 4.116 seconds of CPU in a 4.20-second sampled interval and had a 352 MB footprint. Symbolicating Electron Framework 44.4.3 identified the repeated path as: ```text content::FindRequestManager::FinalUpdateReceived(int, content::RenderFrameHost*) content::FindRequestManager::Traverse(content::RenderFrameHost*, bool, bool, bool) content::(anonymous namespace)::GetChildren(content::RenderFrameHostImpl*) content::(anonymous namespace)::GetNextSibling(content::RenderFrameHostImpl*) ``` This appears to be the same class of issue described in [electron/electron#20602](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/20602), where a comment reports an infinite loop in `find_request_manager.cc` with a webview and iframe. That issue is closed, and the problem remains reproducible on Electron 44.4.3. A renderer-side `window.find()` implementation does not hang on the same fixture, which further isolates the failure to the native Electron/Chromium find-in-page path.

— sent via Glean Tau

nodes.title: Linux tray registers a hollow StatusNotifierItem on Electron 43 (no interfaces exported)
nodes.body:
## Environment

- Electron: 43 (Arch Linux system package `/usr/lib/electron43`, Chromium with the StatusNotifierItem multiplexer refactor crrev.com/c/8043132)
- OS: Linux (Hyprland/Wayland session, dbus session bus)
- Also reproduced on: same runtime via `electron43 --no-sandbox`

## Repro

```js
// main.js
const { app, Tray, nativeImage } = require("electron");
app.whenReady().then(() => {
    const img = nativeImage.createFromPath("/path/to/any.png"); // valid 225x225 png, img.isEmpty() === false
    const tray = new Tray(img);
    tray.setToolTip("tray-probe");
});
```

Run with `electron43 main.js`.

## Expected

The tray exports `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem` with Properties (IconName/IconPixmap/ToolTip/...) at its object path, like Electron <= 42.

## Actual

- The app acquires `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` and registers with the watcher (`RegisteredStatusNotifierItems` gains `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1/StatusNotifierItem/1/StatusNotifierItem`).
- The object at `/StatusNotifierItem/1/StatusNotifierItem` exists but is an **empty node**: no `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem` interface, no `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties` (`gdbus introspect` returns `node /StatusNotifierItem/1/StatusNotifierItem {};`, property Get fails with `Method \"Get\" ... doesn't exist`).
- It never fills in — the item stays hollow for the app's entire lifetime.
- The same pattern is visible in long-running apps: GoofCord (open source, `new Tray(png); tray.setToolTip()` — nothing exotic) sits in the tray as an image-missing placeholder forever on Electron 43, while the same apps work with older Electron builds (Signal/Ferdium ship their own).

Verbose startup logging (`--enable-logging --v=1`) shows the dbus layer retrying during init (`GetNameOwner` storm, `Filter function already exists`), and name ownership takes ~15s instead of being immediate; no `RequestName`/`RegisterStatusNotifierItem` method calls are visible in the `dbus/bus.cc` method-call trace, suggesting the multiplexer/registration path runs somewhere the verbose log doesn't cover.

## Impact

Any Electron-43 app using `Tray` on Linux shows a broken/placeholder tray icon in StatusNotifierItem hosts (tested against AstalTray's watcher). The registration also never gets reaped when the app dies because it is keyed by the combined name/path string (reported separately to AstalTray as Aylur/astal#485, now with a known producer).

Happy to run any diagnostics against the live system.

nodes.title: Crash (SIGTRAP) on drag-and-drop of a file whose filename contains a non-ASCII character (U+2014) — Linux/Wayland
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [X] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### AI Disclaimer As can be seen the document below was written by an AI-Agent, it was not working autonomously though. /Alex ### Electron Version 44.4.3 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version CachyOS (Arch-based), kernel 7.2.6-1-cachyos, x86_64, KDE Plasma on Wayland ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior Dropping a file onto a window fires the `drop` event and the application receives the file, regardless of what characters the file's name contains. ### Actual Behavior If the dropped file's **name** contains a non-ASCII character (tested with U+2014 EM DASH), the Electron process dies immediately with **SIGTRAP**. No `dragenter`, `dragover` or `drop` handler ever runs, and nothing is logged. A byte-identical copy of the same file with an ASCII-only name is dropped and handled normally, so the file's contents, size and format are not involved — only its name. Tested in both directions repeatedly; it is 100% consistent. Chromium 152 on the same machine, with an equivalent drop target on a local page, accepts the same em-dash file without any problem. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information **Minimal reproduction** (three files): `package.json` ```json { "name": "repro", "version": "1.0.0", "main": "main.js", "private": true } ``` `main.js` ```js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron'); app.whenReady().then(() => { const w = new BrowserWindow({ width: 760, height: 520, webPreferences: { nodeIntegration: true, contextIsolation: false } }); w.loadFile('index.html'); }); app.on('window-all-closed', () => app.quit()); ``` `index.html` ```html
drop a file here
``` Steps: 1. `touch "repro — test.md"` — the separator is U+2014 EM DASH (bytes `e2 80 94`). 2. `cp "repro — test.md" repro-test.md` 3. `npm i electron && ./node_modules/.bin/electron .` 4. Drag `repro-test.md` onto the window → logs `dropped repro-test.md`. Works. 5. Drag `repro — test.md` onto the window → the process exits with SIGTRAP; no handler runs.
In-depth investigation

systemd-coredump for the crash in the minimal app above: ``` Signal: 5 (TRAP) si_code: SI_KERNEL Stack trace of thread 60221 (main thread): #0 0x0000562ad9e364c0 n/a (electron + 0x839c4c0) #1 0x0000562ad9f889ee n/a (electron + 0x84ee9ee) #2 0x0000562ad9f895c6 n/a (electron + 0x84ef5c6) #3 0x0000562ada045484 n/a (electron + 0x85ab484) #4 0x0000562ada156245 n/a (electron + 0x86bc245) #5 0x0000562ada155fcb n/a (electron + 0x86bbfcb) #6 0x0000562ada155e65 n/a (electron + 0x86bbe65) ``` (unsymbolized — stock stripped release binary) I originally hit this in Discord 1.0.158, which ships Electron 42.11.1: attaching any file with an em dash in its name kills the client instantly, before the upload begins (its `renderer_js.log` shows no `CloudUpload` entry for the failing file, while ASCII-named files in the same session log the normal upload sequence). Discord's Crashpad dumps show the same signature — `SIGTRAP` at `0x0`, `ptype=utility` — with `libgtk-3`, `libgdk-3`, `libgdk_pixbuf-2.0`, `libglycin-2` and `libtinysparql-3.0` loaded in the crashing process. Because of that module list I first suspected the known gdk-pixbuf ≥ 2.44.1 / glycin / `bwrap` crash class (GNOME/gdk-pixbuf#292), where a failing glycin loader leads to a fatal GTK assertion. That appears **not** to be it: `app.getFileIcon()` resolves the same em-dash paths without error (tested on both the `.md` and a `.pdf`), so the icon/thumbnail path is not implicated. Environment: gtk3 1:3.24.52, gdk-pixbuf2 2.44.7, glycin 2.1.5, bubblewrap 0.12.0, xdg-desktop-portal 1.22.1 with both -gtk 1.15.3 and -kde 6.7.5 installed. Not tested: X11, other distributions, other non-ASCII codepoints (only U+2014 so far).

nodes.title: Tray icon does not visually update on GNOME while the app is unfocused (NewIcon signal fires correctly)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.7.1 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, GNOME Shell 50.1 (Wayland session; app launched with `--ozone-platform=x11`) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ - not a regression as far as I can tell, seems to affect this Electron version and possibly others. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior After calling `tray.setImage()` with a new icon while the app's `BrowserWindow` is unfocused, the tray icon in the top panel updates immediately, the same as it does when the app is focused. ### Actual Behavior The tray icon often stays on the previous image while the app is unfocused, and only catches up once the window regains focus (or some other event forces GNOME Shell to repaint the top panel). ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/oalfroukh/5a3d7677823db53c9b4b05c2d3ced221 ### Additional Information Run the gist with `electron . --ozone-platform=x11`. It creates a window, waits 3s, blurs the window, waits 1s, then calls `tray.setImage()` with a different (red) icon while `win.isFocused()` is `false`. On GNOME Shell with the `ubuntu-appindicators` extension, the icon frequently does not turn red until the window is refocused.
In-depth investigation

I ran `dbus-monitor --session "interface='org.kde.StatusNotifierItem'"` alongside the repro and confirmed Electron emits `NewIconThemePath` and `NewIcon` on the `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem` interface correctly every time `tray.setImage()` is called, including while the window is unfocused - captured a signal timestamped well after `win.isFocused()` was already `false`. `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get` on `IconName` also reflects the new icon name immediately, unfocused or not. So Electron's side of the StatusNotifierItem protocol appears correct in both the signal and the property value. The GNOME `ubuntu-appindicators` extension (https://github.com/ubuntu/gnome-shell-extension-appindicator) seems to not always repaint the panel icon in response to `NewIcon` alone while the associated window is unfocused, though I haven't dug into that extension's source to confirm why. I'm filing this against Electron rather than the extension because: this pattern (GNOME AppIndicator/StatusNotifierItem quirks) has come up in several Electron issues before (#52674, #53213, #53138), so the team may already be aware of extension-side flakiness like this, and may know of a workaround Electron could apply (e.g. re-emitting the icon signals on focus/blur, or another pattern that happens to be more reliable against this consumer) even though the root cause is outside Electron's own code.
Have you tested it with Electron v43.2.0? To confirm it's related to recent SNI changes or not.

Tested with 43.2.0 as requested, plus 43.7.1, across a minimal repro app packaged four different ways (raw dev binary, `.deb`, Flatpak) — this symptom is intermittent on every version and every packaging format I tried, not something that looks specific to 43.3+/recent SNI changes as far as I can tell. New finding since the original report: it correlates with a desktop notification firing while the window is unfocused. I reproduced it live on two completely unrelated apps at once (a our app dev build and a throwaway test app) right after a notification arrived, including from a plain `notify-send` with nothing to do with either app. It's not deterministic though — repeating the same notification-then-icon-swap sequence sometimes shows the new icon fine and sometimes doesn't. Also found: once *any* window on the system gains focus — not necessarily the tray-owning app's own window — the icon catches up immediately. That points at GNOME Shell doing some kind of broader repaint pass on focus-change events that incidentally catches whatever AppIndicator icons are currently stuck, rather than anything about Electron's own signal emission (which I already confirmed separately is always correct, every time, regardless of any of this).
In-depth testing today

- Electron 43.2.0 (raw dev binary, unsandboxed): 12/12 clean icon swaps in an automated test, no stuck icon. - Electron 43.7.1 (raw dev binary, unsandboxed): 12/12 clean swaps, twice, in separate runs. - Electron 43.7.1 packaged as `.deb` (installed, unsandboxed): clean in an initial click-driven test, but intermittent misses once combined with a real notification (e.g. trial 3 of a later 8-trial batch clearly missed). - Electron 43.7.1 packaged as Flatpak: same intermittent pattern — clean in some runs (12/12 automated swaps, 14/14 manual clicks while unfocused), but reproduced the stuck state live via a real app notification arriving while the window was unfocused, at the same moment as a separate, unrelated Flatpak test app also got stuck. - A completely generic `notify-send` (unrelated to either app, no Electron involved in sending it) reproduced the stuck state too, ruling out anything app-specific about the notification itself. - Recovery: confirmed multiple times that focusing an unrelated window (not the tray-owning app) unsticks it immediately, for both apps at once. So: no evidence of a 43.2 vs 43.3+ difference for this specific symptom, and no evidence it's tied to a particular packaging format (unsandboxed/`.deb`/Flatpak all show it). It looks environment/timing-dependent — something inside GNOME Shell's `ubuntu-appindicators` extension racing with notification-banner rendering — correlated with, but not deterministically caused by, a notification appearing while the app is unfocused.

In that case, it looks like the issue is unrelated to Electron if I get it right? You might want to seek for Ubuntu help since AppIndicators is their project.

Furthermore, you can also test Chrome's tray icon with extensions like [this](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/chrome-background-runner/cfpbjggdmogjceodagocpbmikhdoaokn) (it makes Chrome create tray icons too), to see if it's Electron-specific or all Chromium-based are affected.

Tried both of your suggestions — both came back inconclusive, for reasons unrelated to the bug itself, so wanted to report that honestly rather than go quiet.

**Chrome's tray icon**: tried this twice, including with the exact extension you linked (Chrome Background Runner). In both cases, closing the window either fully quit Chrome with no tray icon, or left the process alive in the background with still no tray icon at all. Best I can tell, whatever background-app/system-tray feature that relies on doesn't exist (or isn't reachable) in the Chromium build available on this system, so I wasn't able to get a comparable test running at all — not a "it works fine" result, just "couldn't test it here."

**Going further than Chrome**: to rule out Chromium as a factor entirely (not just Electron), I also wrote a minimal StatusNotifierItem D-Bus service by hand — no Electron, no Chromium, no GTK/libappindicator, just the raw protocol, the same one Electron implements internally. It registers successfully with the watcher and emits the correct `NewIcon`/`NewIconThemePath` signals on schedule, but the icon doesn't render at all under this system's GNOME AppIndicator extension, even under normal baseline conditions with no notification involved. So that's inconclusive too — most likely a gap in my minimal implementation rather than new evidence either way, and not something I want to over-interpret.

Given both of those hit dead ends, I'll stand by what was already reported: reproduced live on two completely unrelated apps at once right after a real notification, reproduced with a plain `notify-send` alone (nothing to do with either app), recovers as soon as any unrelated window gains focus, and shows the same intermittent pattern across two Electron versions and three packaging formats (unsandboxed, `.deb`, Flatpak). Happy to try anything else that would help narrow it down further.

> So that's inconclusive too — most likely a gap in my minimal implementation rather than new evidence either way, and not something I want to over-interpret.

Lol no, you proved it was an issue specific to your distro / WM. Not an electron bug. Your responses appear to be entirely AI driven with no real thought behind them. Closing this out as an issue with your system

nodes.title: Support macOS system Password AutoFill providers for HTML credential fields
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

On macOS, standard HTML username/password fields in an Electron application do not appear to participate in the system Password AutoFill experience, even when a credential provider is configured at the OS level.

For example, given:

```html
<input
  type="text"
  name="username"
  autocomplete="username"
/>

<input
  type="password"
  name="password"
  autocomplete="current-password"
/>
```
the same page produces different behavior depending on where it is rendered:

Environment | Result
-- | --
Safari, macOS AutoFill provider configured | System Password AutoFill offered the configured provider
Chrome, provider's browser extension enabled | Browser extension offered credentials
Chrome, browser extension disabled | No system Password AutoFill suggestion
Electron | No system AutoFill suggestion

*These tests were performed with 1Password as the configured macOS AutoFill provider*

In this test, Electron did not provide the native macOS Password AutoFill experience that Safari provided for the same semantic HTML fields.

This came up while using pgAdmin 4 Desktop, which is an Electron application. 1Password Universal Autofill (Cmd+\) works there, but the native inline Password AutoFill experience does not.


### Proposed Solution

Electron apps should be able to use macOS Password AutoFill for standard username and password fields without requiring a browser extension.

For example, fields using standard HTML attributes such as:

```
autocomplete="username"
autocomplete="current-password"
```
should be able to show credentials from password managers configured in macOS, similar to how the same fields behave in Safari.

I’m not sure whether this should be handled in Electron or upstream in Chromium. I’m opening this issue to confirm whether this is something Electron intends to support and, if so, where the change should be made.


### Alternatives Considered

#### 1Password Universal Autofill

In pgAdmin 4 Desktop, which is a signed Electron application, 1Password Universal Autofill using Cmd+\ can fill the credential field. This works, but it is a separate workflow from macOS's native inline Password AutoFill experience and requires the user to know and invoke the shortcut.

#### Browser extensions

When the application is run in Chrome, the 1Password browser extension provides autofill. Electron applications, however, cannot generally rely on users installing browser password-manager extensions.

#### Application-specific password-manager integration

Individual Electron applications could potentially integrate with password managers themselves, but that would require each application to implement provider-specific behavior rather than using the operating system's credential-provider mechanism.

### Additional Information

Minimal test field:

```html
<form>
  <label>
    Username
    <input
      type="text"
      name="username"
      autocomplete="username"
    />
  </label>

  <label>
    Password
    <input
      type="password"
      name="password"
      autocomplete="current-password"
    />
  </label>
</form>
```
Minimal Electron wrapper used for the reproduction:
```js
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron');

function createWindow() {
  const win = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 600,
    height: 400,
  });

  win.loadURL('http://127.0.0.1:8080');
}

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  app.setAccessibilitySupportEnabled(true);
  createWindow();

  app.on('activate', () => {
    if (BrowserWindow.getAllWindows().length === 0) {
      createWindow();
    }
  });
});

app.on('window-all-closed', () => {
  if (process.platform !== 'darwin') {
    app.quit();
  }
});
```
I also reproduced the behavior without `app.setAccessibilitySupportEnabled(true);` enabling it explicitly did not change the Password AutoFill behavior.

Tested on:
```
macOS: 26.5.1 (Tahoe, 25F80)
Electron: 44.4.3
Architecture: arm64
1Password: 8.12.36 (81236040)
Safari: 26.5 (21624.2.5.11.4)
Chrome: 152.0.7977.84 (Official Build) (arm64)
```

<details> 
<summary>In-depth investigation</summary>
I originally encountered this with pgAdmin 4 Desktop and compared its behavior with pgAdmin 4 running in a normal browser.

Accessibility Inspector shows that Electron exposes the password field to macOS as a secure text field:
```
Role: AXTextField
Subrole: AXSecureTextField
Class: BrowserAccessibilityCocoa
```

A minimal Electron test application exposes its password field with the same accessibility role/subrole.

I also tested:
- Electron loaded from `file://`
- Electron loading the same page over `http://127.0.0.1`
- `app.setAccessibilitySupportEnabled(true)`
- a packaged Electron application

The packaged test application was ad-hoc signed. 1Password Universal Autofill did not fill it, which is consistent with 1Password's requirement for a trusted code signature. pgAdmin 4 Desktop, which is normally signed, does support 1Password Universal Autofill via `Cmd+\`.

This suggests the accessibility representation and 1Password Universal Autofill path are separate from the missing inline macOS Password AutoFill behavior.

While looking through the Electron source, I found Electron's autofill-related implementation in:
```
shell/renderer/electron_autofill_agent.cc
shell/browser/electron_autofill_driver.cc
shell/browser/electron_autofill_driver_factory.cc
shell/browser/ui/autofill_popup.cc
```
`ElectronAutofillAgent` implements `blink::WebAutofillClient`, but I did not find an obvious integration for macOS Password AutoFill in Electron’s source.

The only `AuthenticationServices` import I found in the Electron source I searched was associated with the macOS platform-passkey implementation:
`shell/browser/webauthn/electron_platform_passkeys_authenticator_mac.mm`

I also searched for:
```
NSTextContentType
AuthenticationServices
ASCredential
current-password
PasswordManagerClient
```
and did not find an obvious bridge for normal username/password AutoFill.

I have not yet built Electron/Chromium from source because I wanted to confirm with maintainers whether this integration belongs in Electron, upstream Chromium, or elsewhere before pursuing an implementation.

</details>

I'm interested in working on an implementation if this is considered in scope for Electron and would appreciate guidance on the appropriate integration point.

nodes.title: [Bug]: Skia GPU shaders are never persisted to disk (no GetGrShaderDiskCacheDirectory / GetShaderDiskCacheDirectory override)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. (Closest: #10072 from 2017, a different key-prefix problem; #40366 / #40475 concern the WebGL `GPUCache`.) ### Electron Version 42.10.1 (Chromium 148.0.7778.280). The missing override has been missing since Skia's shader cache got its own handle, so every supported version. ### What operating system(s) are you using? Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 26200; Intel Iris Xe, driver 30.0.101.1298 (ANGLE / D3D11) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version None. The override has never existed in this repository. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No. Chrome and Edge write `User Data\GrShaderCache` and `User Data\ShaderCache` and hit them on the next launch. ### Expected Behavior Shaders that Skia compiles for the display compositor and OOP raster are persisted between launches, like Chrome, so the second launch of an app does not pay for compiling them again. ### Actual Behavior They are never written. Every launch of every Electron app recompiles every shader its UI touches, on the GPU main thread, before the first frame can be presented. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Skia compiles a program
GrShaderCache::store"] --> B["GpuChannelManager::StoreShader
→ StoreBlobToDisk(kGrShaderGpuDiskCacheHandle)"] B --> C{"path registered for
kGrShaderGpuDiskCacheHandle?"} C -->|"Chrome / Edge"| D["ChromeContentBrowserClient::GetGrShaderDiskCacheDirectory()
→ User Data\\GrShaderCache ✅"] C -->|"Electron"| E["ContentBrowserClient default → empty path
→ no cache for the handle → blob dropped ❌"] ``` - `content/browser/gpu/gpu_disk_cache_factory.cc` maps `kGrShaderGpuDiskCacheHandle` → `GetContentClient()->browser()->GetGrShaderDiskCacheDirectory()` and `kDisplayCompositorGpuDiskCacheHandle` → `GetShaderDiskCacheDirectory()`, and only registers a cache when the path is non-empty. - `content/public/browser/content_browser_client.cc`: both defaults return `base::FilePath()`. - `shell/browser/electron_browser_client.{h,cc}` override neither (0 hits for `ShaderDiskCache` in this repository). - `gpu/ipc/service/gpu_channel_manager.cc`: `StoreShader` always targets `kGrShaderGpuDiskCacheHandle`, and loads for that handle are the only ones that reach `GrShaderCache::PopulateCache`. The per-renderer `GPUCache` that Electron apps do have feeds `gles2::ProgramCache` (WebGL programs) instead — which is why VS Code's has ~1,200 entries and a non-WebGL app's has 0. Measured on this machine with `--trace-startup` on the first launch of a shell that paints text, rounded rects and shadows, identical on each traced launch: | GPU main thread, first raster of the UI | per launch | |---|---| | `GrShaderCache::load` | 31, all misses | | `GrShaderCache::store` | 31 | | `Program::MainLinkLoadEvent::wait` (ANGLE → `D3DCompile`) | 31 × ~15 ms = **~480 ms**, serialised | | frames presented meanwhile | 0 | | `sessionData/GrShaderCache` after 40 s and a clean exit | does not exist | Same on disk for other apps installed here: | | `GrShaderCache` | `ShaderCache` | `GPUCache` entries | |---|---|---|---| | Chrome, Edge | present | present | (per profile) | | VS Code | absent | absent | 1,223 (WebGL) | | Slack, Discord | absent | absent | present | | this app | absent | absent | 0 | ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/Hona/0ba82a4c26cc576cb4caeebc3f4ec746 — loads a page with a few paint ops, waits 10 s, then prints which shader cache directories exist under `sessionData` and how many entries their index reports. `GrShaderCache` / `ShaderCache` are `absent` on every run; in Chrome the equivalent directories fill up. ### Additional Information Proposed fix, mirroring `ChromeContentBrowserClient`: ```cpp // shell/browser/electron_browser_client.cc base::FilePath ElectronBrowserClient::GetShaderDiskCacheDirectory() { return SessionDataPath().Append(FILE_PATH_LITERAL("ShaderCache")); } base::FilePath ElectronBrowserClient::GetGrShaderDiskCacheDirectory() { return SessionDataPath().Append(FILE_PATH_LITERAL("GrShaderCache")); } ``` where `SessionDataPath()` is whatever resolves `app.getPath("sessionData")` (the same root the existing `GPUCache` lands in). `GetGraphiteDawnDiskCacheDirectory()` and, on platforms where `features::kGpuPersistentCache` is on, `GetGPUPersistentCacheDirectory()` have the same shape. `session.clearStorageData({ storages: ["shadercache"] })` and the `sessionData` docs would need to cover the new directories. Happy to send the PR.

<!-- issue-template-check -->

Hello @Hona. Thanks for taking the time to open an issue and helping to make Electron better!

This issue was automatically closed because its body does not follow any of this repository's issue templates. Maintainers rely on the sections in those templates to triage issues, and issues that are missing them usually cannot be acted upon.

nodes.title: macOS: setBounds with huge numbers like -1e10 crashes the app
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.4.2 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 15 (darwin 24.6.0) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior Calling `win.setBounds({ x: -1e10, y: -1e10, width: 400, height: 300 })` should not crash the app. A bad number should throw a JavaScript error or be ignored. `try/catch` should work. The process should keep running. ### Actual Behavior On macOS the process dies. `setBounds` often returns as if it succeeded. A moment later the app exits with SIGTRAP (133). JavaScript `try/catch` does not catch this. The crash looks like: ``` NSInternalInconsistencyException Invalid parameter not satisfying: CGRectContainsRect( CGRectMake((CGFloat)INT_MIN, (CGFloat)INT_MIN, (CGFloat)INT_MAX - (CGFloat)INT_MIN, (CGFloat)INT_MAX - (CGFloat)INT_MIN), frame) self= frame={{-2147483648, ...}, {0, 0}} ``` `-2147483648` is `INT_MIN`. That is not the `-1e10` passed from JavaScript. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/xia-chao/c6d8ef8bb82dea48ae4e1c3260c9234b ### Additional Information How to reproduce on Electron 44.4.2 (macOS arm64): 1. Create a hidden `BaseWindow`. 2. Call `setBounds` with `x` and `y` set to `-1e10` (`-10000000000`). This is a finite number, not `NaN` or `Infinity`. 3. Repeat that call about 40 times. 4. Wait a short time (the assert often fires on a later AppKit tick, after `setBounds` has already returned). ```js const { app, BaseWindow } = require('electron'); app.whenReady().then(() => { const w = new BaseWindow({ show: false, width: 400, height: 300 }); for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) { w.setBounds({ x: -1e10, y: -1e10, width: 400, height: 300 }); } setTimeout(() => app.quit(), 800); }); ``` Fix in progress: https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/54101 **1. Breakpoint at `ToRoundedRect`. Locals already show `x` / `y` = `-1e+10`.** **2. Call stack: JS `setBounds` is inside the C++ rect converter.** **3. Debug console: normal bounds first, then the trigger `-10000000000`.** **4. After continue: AppKit asserts on an `INT_MIN` frame, process SIGTRAP.**
In-depth investigation

On Electron 44.4.2, `gin::Converter::FromV8` calls `ToRoundedRect`. A finite value like `-1e10` saturates to `INT_MIN` on float-to-int conversion. `NativeWindowMac::SetBounds` clamps size, not origin, then calls `[window_ setFrame:]`. AppKit asserts and the process dies. An `isfinite`-only check would still accept `-1e10`.

<!-- issue-template-check -->

This issue was automatically closed because its body does not follow any of this repository's issue templates. Maintainers rely on the sections in those templates to triage issues, and issues that are missing them usually cannot be acted upon.

To get this issue triaged, please either:

_No response_

No

### Expected Behavior

Apologies in advance for the peculiar bug-report, but this truly appears to be an Electron related issue...

Setup is as follows: Laptop with an internal 2.8k-screen, variable refresh rate (VRR) enabled; an external 4k-monitor (its VRR state seems irrelevant). Both screens are in-use.

Run two Electron-based apps; one on either monitor; both of their windows maximised (not full-screen).

I would expect the (drawing) performance of both applications to be identical, and to be good/"smooth".

### Actual Behavior

It is not.

Performance of the maximised window on the laptop's screen is terrible (feels like "15 FPS"). The moment the Electron app on the other/external monitor goes from maximised to windowed, performance of the maximised window on the laptop screen returns to normal.

In other words: Performance is as expected in all situations, _except_ when two Electron-based apps run with maximised windows on the two separate monitors (where one has VRR enabled; the VRR state of the other screen seems not to matter).

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This screen capture illustrates the problem perhaps better than the above description:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e196983-8714-4386-ba6c-0e45d8142703

The effect is diminished in the capture as a result of the load put on the system by capturing. The difference in v-sync performance is still pretty obvious though. The external monitor is on the top left, the laptop's screen on the bottom right.

Identical behaviour is observed with other (recent) Electron apps (Joplin, Electron 42; Slack, Electron 44). VS Code offers the easiest reproduction as one can simply run [vsynctester.com](https://www.vsynctester.com/) in its internal browser. Any combination of VS Code, Joplin, and Slack (so I would assume "any" Electron-based app) can be used to reproduce the issue.

The problem does not occur with Chromium itself (tested with ungoogled-chromium `152.0.7977.82`), nor with other applications (i.e., Firefox works fine too).

Disabling VRR on the laptop's screen resolves the issue.

The converse setup (laptop screen with VRR disabled; 4k-monitor with VRR enabled) doesn't exhibit the issue either. Perhaps a result of the difference in VRR ranges?

- 4k-monitor: 48-120 Hz

nodes.title: ready-to-show never fires for hidden windows with titleBarOverlay on Windows (regression in 44.4.x)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

44.4.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 (10.0.26200)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

44.1.1

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A `BrowserWindow` created with `show: false` emits `ready-to-show` after its first paint, so the window can be shown without a flash — this works on 44.1.1.

### Actual Behavior

On 44.4.1 the event never fires, so an app that waits for `ready-to-show` to call `show()` stays invisible forever. The page itself loads normally (`did-finish-load` fires, the renderer is alive, CDP works). To end users the app appears not to start. This broke our released Windows build for every user.

Output of the testcase on both versions:

```
electron 44.1.1 / Chromium 152.0.7977.65: RESULT ready-to-show=true did-finish-load=true
electron 44.4.1 / Chromium 152.0.7977.78: RESULT ready-to-show=false did-finish-load=true
```

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/huang-sh/eec4ca48656c393bd275dc605af55673

### Additional Information

Bisecting the window options on 44.4.1:

- Removing `titleBarOverlay` makes `ready-to-show` fire again — the overlay on an initially-hidden window is what suppresses it.
- `backgroundThrottling: false` and `webviewTag: true` are not involved (both fire fine without the overlay).
- Only verified on Windows; not tested on macOS/Linux.

Workaround we shipped: fall back to showing the window from `did-finish-load` after a short delay. Happy to test a fix build on short notice.

<!-- issue-template-check -->

Hello @huang-sh. Thanks for taking the time to open an issue and helping to make Electron better!

This issue was automatically closed because its body does not follow any of this repository's issue templates. Maintainers rely on the sections in those templates to triage issues, and issues that are missing them usually cannot be acted upon.

To get this issue triaged, please either:

* Edit the issue body above to include all of the sections from one of our [issue templates](https://github.com/electron/electron/tree/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE) - it will be reopened automatically once it does, or
* File a new issue via https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/new/choose, which will fill in the correct template for you.

Thanks for reporting!

Would you be able to check which v44 minor or patch version introduced the issue?

Bisected on Windows 11 (10.0.26200, x64) with the testcase gist above:

| Electron | Chromium | `ready-to-show` |
|---|---|---|
| 44.1.1 | 152.0.7977.65 | ✅ fires |
| 44.2.0 | 152.0.7977.76 | ✅ fires |
| 44.3.0 | 152.0.7977.78 | ✅ fires |
| **44.4.0** | 152.0.7977.78 | ❌ never fires |
| 44.4.1 | 152.0.7977.78 | ❌ never fires |
| 44.4.2 | 152.0.7977.130 | ❌ never fires (still broken in latest) |

**Introduced in v44.4.0.** The key comparison: 44.3.0 and 44.4.0 ship the *same* Chromium (152.0.7977.78) but flip behavior, so this is an Electron-side change, not Chromium.

One entry in the [v44.4.0 release notes](https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/tag/v44.4.0) stands out given the `titleBarOverlay` dependency of the repro:

> Fixed Window Controls Overlay CSS environment variables and `navigator.windowControlsOverlay` not being populated for `WebContentsView`s in a `BaseWindow`. [#53812](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/53812)

Suspecting that WCO population change is what suppresses the first-paint signal for initially-hidden overlay windows.
